body.summary: A thread, a blessing and a promise to care for one another.

why.text: Raksha Bandhan celebrates bonds of care through the tying of a protective thread.
The observance falls on Shravana Purnima; use the local window shown in Today.
Aparahna is traditionally preferred, with Bhadra excluded from the chosen window.
The Bali protection verse is a traditional invocation, not proof of one historical origin for every rakhi custom.

gather.text: Rakhi or clean cotton thread, a small plate, roli and rice.
A small sweet or fruit; a safely placed diya if used in your family.

budget.text: Use a simple cotton thread and an offering already at home.
A handwritten promise of care can accompany the thread; an expensive gift is unnecessary.

steps.text: Prepare the plate and gather during the listed local window.
Offer a brief prayer to your family's deity.
Apply tilak and rice if customary, and tie the thread gently.
Exchange blessings and share a sweet or fruit.

who_should_eat.text: This guide does not prescribe a compulsory fast. Follow your own family observance.

dont.text: Avoid the Bhadra interval if your tradition follows that restriction.
Do not tighten the thread enough to hurt the wrist.

texts.title: Traditional protection invocation
texts.devanagari:
येन बद्धो बली राजा दानवेन्द्रो महाबलः।
तेन त्वामभिबध्नामि रक्षे मा चल मा चल॥
texts.iast: yena baddho balī rājā dānavendro mahābalaḥ | tena tvām abhibadhnāmi rakṣe mā cala mā cala ||
texts.meaning: With the protection thread that bound mighty King Bali, I bind you. May this protection remain steady.
texts.source: Traditional raksha-sutra invocation · Dipika ritual booklet
